underTargetReason: The nine exact Search Console queries defined a bounded ROV, underwater-inspection and LARS universe of 21 unique screened organizations. Eight cleared candidate gates, five remained research-required, and eight were duplicate, out-of-scope, no-concrete-offering or unresolved foreign-umbrella exclusions. Expanding outside that universe merely to reach 40 prospects or 10 candidates would pad the run.

unresolvedTrails: Mako Diving: The official site and industry-association trail support a plausible operating identity and ROV-related service, yet they do not establish a current model-specific capability, named deployment or sufficiently precise Canadian operating footprint for review-safe staging.

Dominion Divers (2003): The procurement, association and industry-publication trails do not conclusively separate the legal entity, current website, operating location and lifecycle of Dominion Divers (2003) from Dominion Diving Ltd.; staging either identity would risk an unsafe duplicate or conflation.

Advanced Subsea: The official website and legacy equipment PDFs support an ROV-related offer but do not close a current Canadian legal identity or operating footprint, and no independent recent customer, contract or program record was recovered for the same entity.

DEEPSIX: Official project material supports a real subsea operator, while the corporate-registry lane points to a United Kingdom corporate trail and no durable source establishes a separate Canadian operating entity eligible for this Canada-first run.

DiveLink: The official website and provincial registry trail do not conclusively connect the current brand, legal company, active status and any model-specific ROV capability; no independent current deployment source was recovered after three lanes.
exhaustionEvidence.note: The bounded nine-query universe was screened across official identity, technical, government or procurement, customer or partner, industry or registry, bilingual and broad-web lanes. Repeated names, foreign umbrellas and unrelated dive contractors were not used as filler; the final complementary lanes produced only low or zero decision-useful yield.
